_comment: The Fleets screen - orion2re SCREEN_FLEET (4), FLT1::Fleet_Screen_ (flt1.cpp:486-837). Work order 134, 18 September 2026. Every native rectangle this screen is laid out from lives in screens/fleets/fltgeom.py with its own source line, NOT here: a coordinate in two files is decision 5's exact failure. This file holds the frame, the wording HD has to supply because the original draws it as artwork, and the marks.

frame._note: **HD INVENTION — the native Fleets screen has no frame like this.** FLEET.LBX entry 0 (Draw_Fleet_Screen_, flt1.cpp:385) is flat blue plates with thin bevels; this metal frame with chamfered, orange-lit holes is OrionLayer's own and is not a transcription of anything. Work order 151, Data's chosen layout (_src/fleets_frame_4k_map165.png, sha256 92f89a8650684de237730248a8b3b977674bbe9886a83bc2a961acdbe498a83d), on the 3840x2160 SOURCE CANVAS (decision 69) and stretched over the reference area by _scale_frame, so its holes coincide with the boxes measured out of them. The art arrives with NO ALPHA and all seven buttons unlit; tools/fleets_frame_build.py is the only thing that touches the pixels and does three things to them — Support and Combat rebuilt unlit (151), the RESHAPE of work order 153, and the 32 openings cut. **WORK ORDER 153 CHANGED THE PROPORTIONS AND NOT THE SOURCE**: the map hole gives 195 px of height to the ship panel (1812x1101 -> 1491x906, aspect 1.6458 kept) and 321 px of width to the right column, whose cells, buttons and scroll-bar area are rebuilt at their new size by the piecewise 3-slice in tools/fleets_frame_reshape.py — corners, chamfers, brackets and V-notches are anchors copied pixel for pixel and only measured straight runs are resampled. The cells are 341x221 where they were 261x219; the two extra rows are the opening detector reaching the paint's own edge on a wider row and are explained at fleets_frame_reshape.TARGET_CELL_SIZE. It replaces work order 146's fleets_frame_v4.png (1445x811, sha256 4667e86d1405555d1cddce1b5647c3ced43141bf2a2efe5260de29dab6c1b198). IT CUTS 32 HOLES and the boxes come from them (decision 3): tools/frame_holes.py --write with the fleets rule, then tools/fleets_place_boxes.py --write for the six that have no hole. v3 had ONE opening with the native regions seated inside it, which is why frame.opening is gone from this block. The image carries its OWN outer ring, which is not the shared ring other screens wear — see doc/briefs/146-parked-for-data.md. The ring is the one part of the art 153 does not touch. A short bright stroke beside the text panel's bottom-left corner is a known artefact of the source and is left alone.
frame._no_cutouts_note: SUPERSEDED, AND KEPT SO THE CORRECTION IS ON THE RECORD. It said decision 3 does not apply to this screen, that the frame has one hole and that tools/frame_holes.py has no `fleets` rule. All three stopped being true with work order 146: the frame cuts 32 holes, frame_holes has a `fleets` rule that refuses any other shape, and `--write` IS run on it — the smoke test holds every derived box to its hole. tools/fleet_boxes.py is the tool that seated the regions into one opening and it must not be made to run again; what it used to do for the six boxes that still have no hole is now screens/fleets/fltplaced.py, a rule against a hole rather than a remembered rectangle (work order 153).

regions._skin_note: EVERY REGION AND EVERY CONTROL WEARS thin_border, and decision 34 is why. It gives the two skins one meaning each: inner_panel is the 9-slice art and FRAMES PICTURES, thin_border is the rounded blue outline and GROUPS THINGS. All sixteen boxes here group - four panels, a status strip, a scroll column, seven buttons and a text field. The one picture on this screen is the captain's portrait in the ship panel (flt2.cpp:848-866), and it is deliberately NOT a box: its extent is not a constant but animate::Get_Width_/Get_Height_ of the LBX art at (0xF2, 0x11C) = (242, 284), with the highlight frame two pixels outside it at (0xF0, 0x11A) = (240, 282). A box would have to invent a size. When the portrait is drawn it gets inner_panel, from the art's own size, and not before.
regions._editable_note: All sixteen are F5-editable. The seat in fltgeom is a starting point and not a cage: it places the original's own rectangles, as one group under ONE factor, in the middle of the opening. Drag any of them and the screen follows, because nothing recomputes a rect the file holds - the scroll column's three parts and the twenty icon cells are the only derived geometry and both follow their box (fltgeom.scroll_parts, fltgeom.icon_cells).

words._note: OUR WORDING for the seven controls. The original has no string for any of them: Add_Button_Field_ is called with an empty label and the word is painted into the LBX artwork the field points at (flt1.cpp:1188, :1195, :1201, :1236, and the two Add_Radio_Button_Field_ calls :1257-1258). Decision 38 sends everything the game DOES have a string for through the player's own ESTRINGS/HESTRNGS; these seven have none, so they live here. The hotkeys beside them are the engine's and are not wording: S, A, ESC, -, +, comma, period, R, L, U, C.
words._hint_note: OUR WORDING for the two areas HD leaves empty, decision 15 — the text is here and the box that shows it is a `text` box in boxes.json (decision 37), so neither the words nor the position is in a renderer. Both are marked OMISSION in `marks` below.
words.status_hint: Hover a stack in the game window
words._panel_more_note: OUR WORDING, decision 15. The marker the ship panel draws in place of its last line when even the smallest size does not fit the box. `{n}` is replaced by a count; the substitution is a `replace` and not `str.format`, as decision 37 requires, so a brace in a translated label cannot raise inside the render path. NOTHING ABOUT F5 IN IT: this is on the player's screen and the editor is not the player's business (Data, 20 September 2026). What a developer needs — which box, how many lines, at what size — goes to the log instead, once per change, from `fltpanel`.

scroll._hd_note: HD EXTENSION — HD DRAWS ITS OWN SCROLL BAR. The original fills a 12 px column with palette colour 0xA6 between two LBX arrows (Fill_FltScrn_Scroll_Bar_, flt1.cpp:260-309), and its thumb position is a pointer value the snapshot does not carry (s_scroll_bar.thumb_center_y). So the bar is drawn from the row HD is showing, in this project's own palette, inside the scroll_column box. The three parts keep the original's proportions (fltgeom.SCROLL_PARTS): arrow, 234-unit track, arrow. The WHEEL is the second half of the same extension and is marked in screen.py: the original has no wheel here, and HD's does not scroll locally - it activates the game's own arrow field, because the list window belongs to the game (decision 46).
scroll._visible_rows_note: TRANSCRIBED: s_scroll_bar.visible_rows = 5 (Initialize_Scroll_Bar_, flt1.cpp:34), which is the grid's five rows of four.

marks.hd_state: BUILT, NOT ACCEPTED. No live acceptance has run against this screen: work order 134's live part is parked (doc/briefs/134-parked-for-data.md).
marks._note: Decision 61. The same sentence stands in the module docstring of screens/fleets/screen.py, in v3_projektstatus.md and in the parked file, and a smoke check fails if it leaves any of them.
marks.omission_inset_map: OMISSION — HD DRAWS THE INSET'S STARS AND NOTHING ELSE. The original's inset is a live galaxy map: MOVEBOX::Add_Galaxy_Map_Fields_2_(15, 52, 305, 182, ...) puts one hidden field per star over it (flt1.cpp:1250, movebox.cpp:504-511) and MAINSCR::Scan_Galaxy_Map_Fields_ turns a click there into a relocation (flt1.cpp:640), a refusal on a black hole (:641) or FLT2::Fltscrn_Move_Ships_ (flt1.cpp:649) — a move order. None of the three is built (doc/briefs/134-parked-for-data.md, items 2 and 3), so a click in the inset sends nothing and changes nothing. The hint box `inset_hint` says so on screen; without it the area reads as dead rather than as unbuilt. There is no screen-level path back to the original picture to send the click to: `wants_original` is driven by the View's state alone, and F12 is the application's render mode, not this screen's.
marks.omission_status_line: OMISSION — HD DRAWS THE HOVERED STAR'S NAME AND NOT THE STATUS MESSAGE, AND DRAWS NOTHING AT ALL WHEN NOTHING IS HOVERED. That last part is a transcription, not a gap: FLT1 calls FLT2::Print_Fltscrn_Scanned_Star_Name_ only under `if (MOX::_galaxy_map_scanned_star > -1)` (flt1.cpp:397), so with no star scanned the original writes the strip not at all and it is empty — which is what the original's own screenshot shows. HD used to fill that emptiness with "Hover a stack in the game window", inventing a line the game never prints; work order 142 D4 removed it. What remains omitted is the MESSAGE: Print_Fltscrn_Scanned_Star_Name_ (flt2.cpp:338-522) chooses one line from HESTRNGS 0x67, 0x69-0x6C, 0x21, 0x6E, 0x6F, 0x70, 0xEB, 0x92-0x94 and 0x73, keyed on MOX::_galaxy_map_scanned_star, which is on no wire (the FLTS block carries `scanned_small` and `scanned_big`, the ICONS under the pointer, not the star), and on SHIPMOVE::Ships_Try_To_Move_To_, whose result is the move preview already marked OMISSION in fltwire. Filling it is not a drawing question: it needs the hovered star on the wire.
marks._ship_picture_lifted: LIFTED, work order 142 D1 — the grid cell drew no ship picture and that was marked an OMISSION here. It now draws SHIPS.LBX `ship_type + colour * 50` (KEN::Do_Get_Ship_Picture_Seg, ken.cpp:451-466) from the player's own installation, extracted by tools/fleet_art_extract.py and decoded at load time by screens/fleets/fltart.py (decision 38). The artwork is still never committed and never shipped (decisions 40 and 42), so a clone without it falls back to the name and the builder's colour; the smoke test forces both states. Kept here rather than deleted because a marking that simply vanishes leaves no record that the thing was ever missing.
marks.deviation_panel_overflow: HD EXTENSION — THE SHIP PANEL SHRINKS, THEN SAYS WHAT IT DROPPED. The original prints the scanned ship's lines with fonts::Print_ at a fixed size and lets the drawing window cut whatever does not fit: Set_Window_(15, 282, 320, 465) (flt1.cpp:402) clips the paragraph silently, and FLT2::Print_Scanned_Ship_Data_ (flt2.cpp:524-747) has no shrink, no wrap and no marker. It also uses TWO COLUMNS — weapons at x 0x17 and specials at x 0xBC, each with its own cursor — where HD stacks both in one, which is why HD runs out of room sooner than the original does. HD wraps and shrinks to fit (decision 30, measured by rendering) and, when even the smallest size does not fit, replaces its last line with `words.panel_more` rather than stopping mid-list. Silently dropping a weapon is the one outcome this screen may not have.
marks.omission_panel_plural: OMISSION — THE WEAPON NAME IS ALWAYS THE SINGULAR. The original prints TECHDATA::_weapons[t].name_plural whenever the count is not one (flt2.cpp:706-711). tools/techname_extract.py takes the `name` field and not the plural one, so the catalogue in this tree has no plural to print. The singular stands: an invented "s" is not the original's word either and is wrong for the first irregular one. Lifting it is a change to the extractor and its format version.
marks.omission_panel_damaged_red: OMISSION — A DAMAGED SPECIAL IS NOT SHOWN IN RED. The original colours it with FLT2::_red_colors when its bit is set in special_device_damage_flags (flt2.cpp:724-731). That field is at @118 by the header route (orion2.h:2847-2868) and is NOT verified: the obvious live check — a damaged device must be a fitted one — held on all 60 ships of the acceptance save and proved nothing, because not one of them had any damage. Decision 23 keeps it out until a save with a damaged ship confirms it.
